name: Alok
title: Alok — developer in Bengaluru
description: Web applications and data tools. Python on the backend, TypeScript on the front end.
intro: I build web applications and data tools. Five of them are below, each with something it measures.

projects.name: Zencrest Realty
projects.summary: A marketing site for a Bengaluru real-estate firm, built and shipped end to end. Every page is static HTML and CSS — no client-side JavaScript ships at all.
projects.detail: All copy lives in a typed content file, so changes don't touch markup. Beyond the code: domain registration, DNS, business email, and a post-launch change round with the client.
projects.alt: Zencrest Realty homepage — navy hero with the headline 'Your trusted real estate partner in Bangalore'

projects.name: Calorie Tracker
projects.summary: A calorie tracker built around Indian subcontinent cuisine, which mainstream trackers cover badly. Photograph a plate and the model names each dish and estimates its nutrition.
projects.detail: The model suggests; the user decides. Nothing enters the log until it's confirmed from a preview. Gemini runs behind two server routes, so the API key never reaches the browser, and the log lives entirely in the browser — no accounts, no backend, no sync.
projects.alt: Calorie Tracker identifying roti with ghee, mixed vegetable sabzi and dry whole lentil sabzi from a photograph, with per-item macros

projects.name: food-price-intel
projects.summary: Forecasts the FAO Food Price Index three months ahead. SARIMA forecasts that beat a naive baseline at one-month horizon, scored with walk-forward validation rather than a single holdout.
projects.detail: Models are tested the way they'd actually be used: fit on what was known at the time, predict forward, move the window, repeat. The app forecasts from the last ingested FAO release, so the horizon trails the present date.
projects.alt: Line chart of the FAO Food Price Index — observed history in blue flowing into a red dashed SARIMA forecast

projects.name: cric-metrics
projects.measureCaption: runs, top scorer in the powerplay
projects.summary: Ball-by-ball IPL 2026 statistics, filterable by team and match phase. Counting stats recompute for the selected phase; whole-innings figures stay whole-innings.
projects.detail: Built from ball-by-ball data rather than match summaries, which is what makes the phase filtering possible at all.
projects.alt: Cricket dashboard showing top five powerplay run-scorers and a strike-rate scatter plot, filtered to Royal Challengers Bengaluru

projects.name: Namma Metro Fare Calculator
projects.summary: Fares between any two stations on Bengaluru's metro network. Computes distance, detects interchanges, and names which stations to change at.
projects.detail: The first substantial web project I deployed. Fares follow BMRCL distance slabs.
projects.alt: Fare calculator showing ₹90 for Whitefield to Bommasandra over 53.29 km, requiring two line changes

about: I'm based in Bengaluru, with a master's in computer networking. I build web applications and data tools, mostly Python on the backend with TypeScript on the front end.
The work I like most is where the hard part is getting something correct and keeping it live, rather than getting it to render once.

practice.heading: Scoped phases
practice.body: Work goes out in phases with a written definition of done for each. It makes progress legible and stops scope drifting quietly.

practice.heading: Verify what shipped
practice.body: I check the built output, the network tab and the live URL before calling something finished. What's deployed is what counts, not what's on my machine.

practice.heading: Correct over time
practice.body: Log entries snapshot the data they were written against. Forecasts are scored on a rolling window. Design decisions that keep something true next month, not just today.
